stories.headline: Islanders forward Kyle Palmieri (ACL, meniscus) out 6-8 months
stories.summary: Islanders forward Kyle Palmieri will miss the next six to eight months after suffering a torn ACL and meniscus in his right knee, the team announced Friday.
stories.body:
New York Islanders veteran forward Kyle Palmieri will miss the next six to eight months with a torn ACL and meniscus in his right knee, the team said Friday.

Palmieri, 35, who has four goals and nine points in 23 games, was moved to injured reserve earlier Tuesday after he was hurt in the second period of the Islanders' 4-2 loss Monday to the Toronto Maple Leafs. Palmieri was going toward the net as he became entangled with Maple Leafs forward Easton Cowan, which led to him sliding toward the net, where the back of his right knee struck the goal post at full speed. He would skate back to the bench but was favoring his right knee.

It will be the second time in almost exactly a year that Palmieri, a Long Island native, has suffered a significant knee injury.

Palmieri tore the ACL in his left knee on Nov. 28, 2025, against the Philadelphia Flyers that saw him miss the remainder of last season. That season saw the seven-time 20-goal scorer open the campaign with six goals and 18 points in 25 games before he was ruled out for the rest of the year.

Losing Palmieri, who was tied for eighth on the team in points, means the Islanders will be without one of the most experienced players in their lineup. They do, however, have several wingers who have already been among their more productive offensive players in a group that features Mathew Barzal, Anthony Duclair, Victor Eklund, Emil Heineman, Simon Holmstrom, Matias Maccelli and Ondrej Palat.

Palmieri's absence comes as the Islanders entered Thanksgiving weekend in a playoff spot. They are third in the Metropolitan Division with five points separating them from the second-place New Jersey Devils while the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes have a seven-point edge on the Devils and a 12-point cushion against the Islanders.

stories.headline: Jaguars WR Parker Washington (shoulder) is 'week-to-week'
stories.summary: Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington will miss Sunday's game against the Titans and perhaps more with a shoulder injury.
stories.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars have ruled out wide receiver Parker Washington for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans due to a shoulder injury he suffered during Thursday's practice.

Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said the team considers Washington "week-to-week" with the injury.

Washington leads Jacksonville with 748 receiving yards and six touchdowns.

Losing Washington adds to the injury woes of the AFC South leaders. It's unclear if running back Bhayshul Tuten will play Sunday as he deals with an injury to his ankle/foot area that he aggravated in last week's loss to the New York Giants.

Coen said Friday that the Jags could "possibly give him a go [against the Titans] but not sure yet."

stories.headline: Qatar GP organisers keen to show world 'real situation' amid safety concerns
stories.summary: Qatar's Formula 1 grand prix is going ahead as planned this weekend, with organisers hoping the event will give fans watching around the world a clearer picture of "the real situation" in the country.
stories.body:
Qatar's Formula 1 grand prix is going ahead as planned this weekend, with organisers hoping the event will give fans watching around the world a clearer picture of "the real situation" in the country.

Qatar's race has been under a cloud of uncertainty for much of the year following America and Israel's bombing of Iran, which prompted retaliatory strikes against Qatar and other countries in the region.

F1 was forced to cancel its April races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia and, despite a cooling of hostilities since, fears of renewed escalation following the U.S. midterms had cast doubt over the Qatar Grand Prix on Nov. 29 and the season finale in Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6.

F1 has consistently maintained it is safe to finish the season in the Middle East, citing government travel advice, the continued validity of travel insurance and assurances from local authorities in both countries.

However, government travel advice continues to reflect concerns over renewed hostilities in the region, with the UK's Foreign Office warning on Nov. 18 that the situation remains "deeply unpredictable and the risk of sudden escalation is high."

The Qatar Motor and Motorcycle Federation (QMMF) hopes this weekend's event will help alleviate lingering concerns overseas about the security situation in the country.

"I think for us living here, we know the real situation," QMMF president Abdul Rahman bin Abdullatif Al Mannai told ESPN and select other publications on Friday.

"We know the environment. I think it was a little bit challenging for people who are outside to see the reality."

He added: "Qatar has been safe for much longer time since this conflict started. As you know, Qatar is a mediator [in the conflict]. We trust our government agencies. You know, they've done a fantastic job."

Of the two F1 races cancelled in April, Bahrain's was rescheduled to take place in Malaysia in October, while Saudi Arabia's was dropped from the 2026 schedule altogether.

Al Mannai said Qatar never considered a similar arrangement to stage its event elsewhere.

- Qatar Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli leads George Russell in first practice

- Charles Leclerc urges Ferrari to find 'solution' after clash with Lewis Hamilton

- George Russell breaks silence on Max Verstappen criticism: 'Amusing'

"To be honest, no. We never thought of it this way," he said. "I think it worked out really well for Bahrain ... But for us in Qatar, no, we did not think about it this way.

"We never stopped our plans for MotoGP or for Formula 1, even when the war started and the conflict started."

The World Endurance Championship cancelled its Qatar race altogether after initially postponing the event in March and subsequently determining it could not be rescheduled in 2026.

Qatar's Lusail circuit, which hosts Formula 1 this weekend, staged a contentious MotoGP round on Nov. 8 despite opposition from several riders and the withdrawal of Yamaha.

Reports of teams being given detailed evacuation plans outlining what to do in the event of a missile attack circulated ahead of the MotoGP race.

Al Mannai said the emergency procedures in place for this weekend's grand prix are no different to those at previous editions of the event.

"The resources are there in case they're needed," he said. "Anything related to emergencies, we have full procedures for every single building to make sure that people are safe. Safety is our top priority every year."

Al Mannai said he felt as though the perception away from Qatar was very different to how people living inside the country feel.

"It was challenging, quite honestly, you know, we cannot deny that," he added. "We believe the most challenging part was the media. We wanted to make sure that the right message, the right image goes out.

"But it was challenging to do that. I think having MotoGP first here, that helped a lot. You know, everybody saw it on TV, and saw the situation."

The prospect of whether all 11 F1 teams would turn up to Middle East races had been a talking point in the paddock over the last couple of months.

Mercedes boss Toto Wolff played down the prospect of a similar boycott in F1 earlier this month, questioning the geopolitical expertise of the MotoGP riders who had spoken out against racing in Qatar and insisting he trusted the guidance F1 had received.

Al Mannai said staging the MotoGP event had been an important milestone for Qatar ahead of the F1 race.

"It was a relief for us when they came and they saw Qatar and they saw the paddock and they started practicing," Al Mannai said. "It was a good accomplishment for us to show the world that we can deliver a big sporting event like MotoGP, especially before Formula 1."

stories.headline: José Mourinho hails Jude Bellingham but refuses Zinedine Zidane comparison
stories.summary: José Mourinho called Jude Bellingham "one of the best players of his generation" on Friday, but refused to compare the England star with Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane.
stories.body:
José Mourinho called Jude Bellingham "one of the best players of his generation" on Friday, but refused to compare the England star with Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane.

Bellingham -- who wears Zidane's No. 5 shirt with Madrid -- scored a stunning goal in the team's 5-1 comeback Champions League win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday, continuing his superb start to the season.

The midfielder's form has helped Madrid keep pace with Barcelona at the top of the LaLiga table, with a three-point gap between the pair going into this weekend's games.

"I don't like to compare players from different generations," Mourinho said in a news conference on Friday when asked to rank Bellingham with Zidane.

"Zidane was one of the best in the world of his generation. Jude is already one of the best players of his generation. I don't like to compare."

Mourinho rested Bellingham for the first half against PSV, only to see his team struggle and go 1-0 down -- and the coach responded by sending on Bellingham at halftime to turn the match around.

Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé are two of the Madrid players who have featured most in LaLiga this season, with 1047 and 1163 minutes respectively.

"The reason Kylian and Jude have played so many minutes isn't their names, or a rule," Mourinho said. "It's their performance. If their performance is incomparable with what another player can do, that makes the difference. We feel what it's like to play with, and to play without, Jude."

- Jude Bellingham: I don't care about the Ballon d'Or

- Jobe Bellingham teases Jude over wonder-goal: 'Off his shin!'

The victory over PSV left Madrid top of the Champions League table on 15 points from five games, but Mourinho wouldn't accept that his side are now among the favourites to win the competition. "It's very early," Mourinho said. "We don't know how the teams will arrive at the key moment, the knockout. Right now the only thing I want is not to play the playoffs.

Mourinho said Trent Alexander-Arnold was unavailable to face Alavés on Saturday with illness, while he insisted that he doesn't want to add to his squad in the January window.

"I don't want anyone to come in, or anyone to leave," Mourinho said. "The door is closed in both ways... I don't want to see news about the market, because I don't want anyone."

stories.headline: Why Walker Kessler is the X factor for Luka Doncic and the Lakers this season
stories.summary: Doncic's first request when he became a Laker? Get an 'A-list' big man. It took a year, but Kessler is that man in Los Angeles.
stories.body:
EVEN INSIDE a busy hotel lobby, one with 30-foot ceilings, a gilded life-sized horse statue, a jungle-gym-looking apparatus covering the bar area and an oversized, magenta, metallic art installation at the front entrance, Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler stands out.

It's late in the evening on Nov. 7.

Dressed in a gray sweatsuit and a black trucker-style baseball cap on an off night in Birmingham, Michigan, Daxton Hotel patrons turn as the 7-foot-2 Kessler walks from the elevator banks to a seat at a four-top table as L.A.'s new man in the middle.

He's used to the attention by now.

"It's the way I'm supposed to be," Kessler told ESPN about his height, which puts him as one of the top 10 tallest players in the NBA. "It's weird for me if my feet didn't hang over the bed -- that would feel uncomfortable with me."

He has looked mighty comfortable right from the start this season, scoring 26 points on 12-for-12 shooting (including 10 dunks), with nine rebounds and two blocks in his Lakers debut in an opening-night rout over Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors.

After the game, he joined the "Inside the NBA" crew and received a stamp of approval from a legendary Lakers center.

"The way you played tonight, you played like the best big man in the league," Shaquille O'Neal told Kessler, who became the first Lakers player since Wilt Chamberlain in 1969 to have that many makes without a miss. "Welcome to the big man alliance."

Just before the segment finished, O'Neal chimed in again.

"I got a new nickname for you," he said. "Your new nickname is, 'Milk Chamberlain.' I love you, Milk."

Though Kessler appreciated O'Neal's compliment, he did push back just a little.

"The Milk Chamberlain is ... I don't think I'm anywhere [close to him] ... I'm not Wilt Chamberlain. But that's clever. It's a funny nickname."

Kessler will, of course, not be expected to match Chamberlain's gaudy production (although Kessler's 66.9% shooting percentage so far in Los Angeles is better than Chamberlain fared in four of his five L.A. seasons).

But after Luka Doncic personally asked for him as his preferred pick-and-roll partner, and the Lakers gave up a bevy of assets to acquire him from the Utah Jazz this summer, he will be expected to play Chamberlain to Doncic's Jerry West and win a championship for the Lakers.

Because after the significant haul the Lakers spent to bring him to L.A., the success of the dawning Doncic era will depend on it.

SLUMPED ON A couch in his Manhattan Beach home, with a fire warming the crisp fall air seeping into the living room and past the open sliding glass door window to his back deck, Doncic takes ownership of the transformative roster move.

"I told them after the season I wanted Walker," Doncic told ESPN of an offseason conversation he had with Rob Pelinka, Lakers president of basketball operations and general manager, and the front office.

"I think he's a really good player," Doncic continued. "Obviously, last season he didn't play. He played like five games. Obviously [Utah] kept him out, but just playing against him in the previous years, it was hard to score. He was protecting the rim, he was dominating the paint. So just after the season, I went to them and said, 'I want Walker.'"

Kessler underwent surgery last November to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder, a procedure and recovery that ended his season -- a helpful development in Utah's race to the bottom of the standings to try to land a top pick in the loaded 2026 NBA draft. (They ended up taking Kansas guard Darryn Peterson at No. 2 after BYU forward AJ Dybantsa went No. 1 to Washington.)

After extension talks between Utah and Kessler stalled last June -- sources told ESPN's Tim MacMahon that the Jazz offered a contract in the range of five years, $140 million -- the Lakers were able to capitalize.

The sides agreed to a sign-and-trade deal on July 1 that would pay Kessler $130 million over four years and send to the Jazz the Lakers' unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, and first-round pick swaps in 2028 and 2030.

"When we talked, they told me it's not going to be easy," Doncic said. "I knew that. But when I heard we're going to get him, I was very happy and excited for the season."

Walker, whose career 2.3 blocked shots per game average is tied with O'Neal and Anthony Davis. and trails only Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's 2.6 per game career mark in Lakers franchise history, was immediately tasked with shoring up a defense that ranked 19th last season.

So far it's working.

L.A. ranks No. 11 in defense during its 15-3 start to the season, and Kessler is a main reason why.

He's fourth in the league in blocks per game this season (2.1) and seventh in rebounds (10.8) and his presence has helped the Lakers rank first in steals per game with 10.6.

"It changes [their defense] immensely," Sacramento Kings coach Doug Christie said of Kessler. "As a perimeter defender, when I know that there's somebody back there that's in that key and they are protecting the rim, it's like having a big brother and all of the sudden, I'm bolstered. I feel super confident.

"I'm shooting gaps, I'm going to be way more aggressive on the perimeter because I know that we're funneling everybody to that player. And Walker is a big guy. He understands the paint, trying to be in there as much as he possibly can."

Still, as smoothly as his first month has gone, Kessler's struggles in a couple of games against his former team show how future opponents could try to neutralize him.

FOUR DAYS AFTER his dominant debut, the milk curdled. Kessler, whose four years in Utah counts as the longest stint he'd spent in any place since middle school, scored only two points and attempted only two shots in the Lakers' 132-123 win in Salt Lake City on Oct. 25.

"Walker obviously is friends with a number of their players, and they told him, 'Our game plan is not allow you to have a single dunk or lob,'" Lakers coach JJ Redick said.

It worked.

But it wasn't just the lack of scoring. Kessler grabbed only seven rebounds, as the Jazz outrebounded the Lakers by 21. And he had more fouls (four) than blocks (one).

"It was a special place for me," Kessler said. "I didn't think it would affect me as much as it did, but it definitely did. ... If we would've lost, it would've been that much worse."

After the game, the Jazz acknowledged their former big man was a focal point.

"We had a game plan," Jazz guard Keyonte George told ESPN. "When he plays at a high level, he raises the floor for a team."

Did his old teammates try to get in his head?

"Human nature, man," George said with a smile. "He left our squad."

The Lakers played the Jazz again on Nov. 18 and lost 109-97. This time, Kessler had 10 points on 3-for-7 shooting, but shot 4-for-10 from the foul line, with 11 rebounds and no blocked shots.

Mo Bamba and Jaxson Hayes -- two former backup centers for the Lakers -- combined for 12 points, 23 rebounds and four blocks.

Redick has challenged the laid-back Kessler, whom Lakers forward Ziaire Williams calls the nicest teammate he has ever had, to play with more of an edge.

"He told me straightforward, 'We need you to be relentless. ... That's your word of the year,'" Kessler said of Redick's message. "And he didn't say it to blow smoke. He was basically just like, 'What is asked of you of this team right now ... we need you to be someone that's just flying around, anchor our defense, rebound the ball, finish opportunities, just do that.'

"And obviously he was like, 'Your game will expand as time goes on, but right now, this is what your staple can be. Your arrival to the Lakers can be stamped by just your motor and your relentless play.'"

His teammates often help him get there.

"If you know him off the court, he's just a really good guy. So a lot of times on the court, you try to get that dog out of him," Lakers forward Jake LaRavia told ESPN.

"A lot of times, I just yell at him to try to get him going. Like, I'll hit him on the chest real hard or just something that wakes him up a little bit and that will kind of get him going."

ANY WESTERN CONFERENCE team signing a 25-year-old center to a multiyear contract in 2026 means that player has to be part of any solution to contend with the 22-year-old dynamo that is the San Antonio Spurs' 7-foot-4 Victor Wembanyama, whom Kessler and the Lakers play Friday night (9:30 p.m. ET on Prime).

"He's an unreal player," Kessler said. "His metrics are ... there's no precedent for it. But for me, what a great opportunity to compete against someone like that and to be bettering yourself to try to overcome that kind of level of player. That's how I look at it."

Kessler is not expected to become a perennial MVP contender to compete with Wembanyama. But L.A. does want him to unlock more options for their offense, and particularly for Doncic in their two-man game.

"Not to talk bad [on Utah], but he didn't play with a player like me that plays a lot of pick-and-roll, sees a lot of stuff on the court," Doncic said. "I still think we got so much improvement left. We're not going to achieve our best in 15 games. ... If our pick-and-roll is going to work, there's going to be a lot of other people open."

Doncic said Redick organized film sessions for him and Kessler during the preseason so they could watch how they were executing the action in practices and scrimmages.

The Lakers already have the NBA's No. 3 offense, up from ninth last season, and that's with three new starters and Reaves sitting out six of the first 18 games.

Doncic says he believes his growing chemistry with Kessler is the key to the unit leveling up.

"When we get good at that," Doncic said of his pick-and-roll with Kessler, "we can be really good."

Being Doncic's chosen teammate to help him win the first title of his NBA career also is motivating.

"To have someone like that, with that pedigree, to say, 'Hey, I want that to be our center' ... it was incredible," Kessler said. "I was like, 'Wow, this dude, he believes in me. He knows that I can help this team.' It makes you excited to play."

And as he gets out of bed every morning in his new Southern California digs and continues to walk in the footsteps of all the great Lakers big men who came before him, he feels right at home.

"I'm where my feet are and I'm here now, a Laker ... " Kessler said. "And I have this opportunity to play on this bigger stage. I know I repeat it a lot, but it's the truth:

"What an opportunity."

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball reactions to MLB offseason trades, signings
stories.summary: Track all the latest MLB free agency and trade news with fantasy baseball analysis from Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell.
stories.byline: Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell
stories.body:
Tracking the offseason MLB trades and signings with fantasy baseball implications for the upcoming season, Eric Karabell and Tristan H. Cockcroft will analyze and provide an outlook for all of the key players involved.

Players were allowed to sign with new teams beginning Nov. 2, although typically things don't really start to heat up until the league's annual winter meetings. This year's meetings are scheduled to take place in San Diego from Dec. 7-9. However, with the current collective bargaining agreement expiring Dec. 1, players and teams alike might end up waiting until after the dust settles on negotiations and a potential lockout before inking any new deals.

In any event, as any contracts are signed or trades get agreed to, this is the place to find all of the fantasy fallout of those deals. Be sure to check back throughout the hot stove season for updates.

Latest updates include the Detroit Tigers signing Kevin Gausman, the Miami Marlins signing Gary Sanchez and the Kansas City Royals signing Alec Bohm.

Below, you will find a list of some of the top free agents at each position. Players labeled with a (Q) received a qualifying offer from their current team and had until Nov. 17 to accept it or decline and become a free agent. Players coming from Japan/Korea who were posted by their current team have a Dec. 1 deadline to reach a deal with an MLB club to play in the United States in 2027.

Note: Not every transaction warrants the attention of fantasy managers, but for those signings and trades that do merit analysis, you'll find them listed below. Players will be separated by position and then listed in chronological order of the move within each positional grouping, with the latest news coming first. Also included are links to any standalone analysis stories and/or videos regarding major free agent signings and trades. Players who end up re-signing with their previous team will not always be included.

Jump to:

Catcher | First base | Second base | Shortstop | Third base

Outfield | DH | Starting pitcher | Relief pitcher

Catcher
Gary Sanchez signs with Marlins
Sanchez, 33, joins his seventh franchise after hitting .209 with 12 home runs as a backup for the champion Brewers. Those statistics may not seem like much, but combined with his 46 walks, and even with only 275 PA, that was enough to make him a top 25 catcher in ESPN points formats. He averaged 1.8 fantasy points per game, better than Salvador Perez, Cal Raleigh and J.T. Realmuto, among others, as only 10 catcher-eligible options drew more walks.

Sanchez should work in tandem with young, lefty-hitting backstop Joe Mack, and it may mean the enticing Agustin Ramirez, a bad catcher but provider of 21 home runs and 16 stolen bases in 2025 (he spent half of 2026 in Triple-A), is not in the team's future plans. -- Karabell (11/25)

Some free agents: Carson Kelly, Kyle Higashioka, James McCann, Travis d'Arnaud, Austin Hedges

First base
Paul Goldschmidt signs with Mets

Goldschmidt, 39, hit only .252 over 380 PA with the Yankees last season -- but how he did so explains why the Mets coveted him. Goldschmidt hit .299/.393/.573 with 11 home runs versus left-handed pitching, one year after posting a .336/.411/.570 line. He has not enjoyed recent success against right-handed pitching. The Mets figure to platoon Goldschmidt, perhaps with lefty-hitting Jared Young. While that should be productive for the team, it isn't so great for fantasy managers.

Goldschmidt finished outside the top 50 first basemen in 2026 scoring. Roster him in daily formats, when you can take advantage of knowing exactly when he will be in the lineup. Fade him in standard leagues. -- Karabell (11/23)

Jake Bauers signs with Red Sox
Bauers, 31, comes off the best season of his journeyman career, posting an .873 OPS with 26 homers and 86 RBIs for the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He admits that he considered retirement as recently as two years ago, but he stuck around for the health benefits. Good timing. Bauers gets a four-year deal with the Red Sox, where he and right-handed-hitting Willson Contreras should make for a formidable 1-2 punch in the middle of the lineup, while sharing 1B/DH duties.

While Bauers was a top-40 hitter in points formats and roto/categories leagues last season, fantasy managers probably shouldn't expect the same kind of production moving forward, even as he performs half the time at hitter-friendly Fenway Park. Bauers had never hit more than 12 home runs in any prior season and, even now, he remains a career .223 hitter with a 2.0 career WAR.

Maybe the solid 16.3% walk rate and .218 ISO will continue, but preliminary results in NFBC drafts have Bauers going just inside the top 150. Perhaps he gets a bump for heading to Boston, but likely only a modest one. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Josh Bell, Ryan Mountcastle, Nathaniel Lowe, Ty France

Second base

Some free agents: Gleyber Torres, Jeff McNeil, Luis Arraez, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Jonathan India, Gavin Lux, Brandon Lowe (Q)

Shortstop
Ha-Seong Kim signs with Tigers
Kim couldn't have had a much worse 2026, from his appearing in only 51 games (primarily due to issues with a finger he injured when he slipped on a sheet of ice in his native Korea in January) to his tying for the third-lowest OPS+ (2) of any player with at least as many as his 147 plate appearances during the divisional era.

The Tigers might have designs on his being their everyday shortstop, but he's more likely to be yet another infielder they can shuffle around -- good news for you Kevin McGonigle keeper/dynasty managers, as it heightens the chances McGonigle will again earn dual qualification at shortstop and third base.

Kim is only a low-end SB option for deep mixed and NL-only rotisserie leagues, barring an absolutely standout spring. -- Cockcroft (11/24)

Other free agents: J.P. Crawford, Mauricio Dubon, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Amed Rosario

Third base
Alec Bohm signs with Royals
Bohm, 30, who attended college at Wichita State in Kansas, heads closer to home after a polarizing seven-season run with the Phillies. Bohm finished runner-up for the 2020 NL Rookie of the Year award, made the 2024 All-Star team and knocked in 97 runs in consecutive seasons, before adding 88 more this past season. Miscast as a power hitter despite his 6-foot-5 frame, Bohm averaged only 14 HRs during the past five seasons in 596 PA, but he piled on RBIs because nearly half his career plate appearances came in the Nos. 4 and 5 lineup spots. Both should continue -- the RBI chances and lineup placement -- in Kansas City.

The Royals coveted a right-handed bat for the middle of their lineup. Bohm, replacing the traded Maikel Garcia at third base, should bat fourth/fifth most of the time, just like he did in Philadelphia. He should knock in runs, just like he did in Philly, because SS Bobby Witt Jr. and others will be on base. Contact-oriented corner infielders are rare in this era. Even so, only 14 third basemen scored more fantasy points in 2026. Bohm has a low strikeout rate, and he performs better versus left-handed pitching, though the change in home ballparks certainly won't help.

Defensively, um, while he made improvement at third base, it's not good news. Fantasy managers generally don't want to know unless it costs the player his starting role -- and that won't be an issue here. Let's just say Kansas City's contact pitchers (like Michael Wacha) will not be pleased by swapping out Gold Glover Garcia for Bohm at the hot corner. -- Karabell 11/25

Teruaki Sato signs with Cubs

Sato, 27 and the defending Nippon Central League Triple Crown winner, reminds many of another left-handed hitting Japanese slugger who came to the United States. Chicago White Sox 1B Munetaka Murakami, who, in his first MLB season, launched 35 home runs with a 16.6% walk rate, albeit with a .207 batting average and 35.4% strikeout rate. Sato is viewed as a better athlete, but expected to offer a similar offensive profile in the "three true outcomes" department, with power, walks and strikeouts.

This profile has value in fantasy, but Murakami averaged only 2.1 ESPN fantasy points per game, outside the top 100 hitters. He was the No. 127 hitter on the Player Rater, even though only nine hitters slugged more home runs. Should potential Sato investors expect better numbers than Murakami's debut? Sato may boast better plate discipline and a better likelihood to adjust his approach, perhaps trading some power for better contact. Fangraphs projects a .247 batting average and 30 home runs. While Murakami is not among ESPN's initial top 200 for points formats, Sato should earn a better ranking, though not among the top 100.

Though Sato is likely ticketed for an outfield corner with the Cubs, he will be eligible at third base only in fantasy drafts based on his games played in Japan in 2026. He can earn additional eligibility with 10 games played at another position in 2027. -- Karabell (11/24)

Royce Lewis traded to Dodgers
Lewis, 27 and a former first-round pick of the Twins in 2017, has long been ticketed for slugging stardom, but his road to becoming one of the premier, power-hitting third basemen has been bumpy. Lewis hit 15 home runs and knocked in 52 over 58 games and 239 PA during his breakout 2023 campaign, with a .920 OPS. Injuries have derailed him since, as Lewis has neither reached 20 home runs in a season nor approached a .800 OPS.

At least Lewis managed to stay healthy enough to reach 500 PA for the first time in 2026, though he struck out in 25.5% of his PA with a career-low 71.9% contact rate. Can the Los Angeles Dodgers get him consistently productive and keep him on the field? The Minnesota Twins clearly could not. Eligible at first base and third base, perhaps the Dodgers view Lewis as a utility option and lefty killer, but if he doesn't hit, it doesn't matter. Bump Lewis up your draft sheets a bit because of this trade, but he remains more of a late-round sleeper than a sure thing. -- Karabell 11/20

Maikel Garcia traded to Mariners

Garcia, 26, suffered through a rough 2026 season, missing months with hamstring and hand injuries, and slugging only .381 during his 82 games and 344 PA. Not that Garcia is a renowned power hitter, but he delivered 16 home runs among his 60 extra-base hits in a breakout 2025, along with 23 stolen bases, after stealing 37 bases in 2024. Garcia missed only seven games during 2024-25, so volume played a role when he finished 18th among hitters in 2025 fantasy points.

A 2025 Gold Glove winner, Garcia is one of the better defensive third basemen in baseball, and he should solidify the position for Seattle. However, while we don't know for sure where he will hit in his new lineup -- and leaving one hitter-challenging home ballpark in Kansas City for another does not help him -- it figures to be near the bottom half, which caps his fantasy upside. Expect Garcia to bounce back to some degree offensively, with his early ESPN 2027 points ranking featuring him positively as the No. 10 3B and just outside the top 100. -- Karabell (11/18)

Other free agents: Eugenio Suarez, Edmundo Sosa, Yoan Moncada, Si Hwan Roh (posted)

Outfield

Some free agents: George Springer, Trent Grisham, Ian Happ, Seiya Suzuki (Q), Randy Arozarena, Taylor Ward, Daulton Varsho, Adolis Garcia, Randal Grichuk, Myles Straw, Lane Thomas

Designated hitter

Some free agents: Joc Pederson, Dominic Smith

Starting pitcher
Kevin Gausman signs with Tigers
Gausman, 35, made 32 starts for the Blue Jays and Cubs in 2026, though his 4.51 ERA and 1.27 WHIP were his worst marks since the 2019 season, and he failed to win double digit games. Blame a spike in home runs and a bit of bad luck, as his BABIP was up 48 points from the prior season.

Gausman remains durable and he is still missing plenty of bats (184 strikeouts). The Tigers need those attributes in filling their rotation, and while fantasy managers may not like the ERA, Gausman was a top 50 starting pitcher in fantasy points thanks to the volume. He should be among the top 50 starters in 2027 drafts as well, with upside for the top 30, just like his prior seasons with Toronto. -- Karabell (11/25)

Toronto Blue Jays sign SP Kaima Taira
Having missed out on their top free-agent pitching prize, Tarik Skubal, the Blue Jays moved quickly to sign Taira, who by many accounts had the second-best raw stuff of any pitcher on this winter's market, to a five-year, $80 million contract. Taira spent seven of his first eight seasons in Japan as a reliever but transitioned beautifully to a starting pitching role in 2026, posting a Nippon Professional Baseball-leading 1.36 ERA across 22 starts and one relief appearance. Prior to that, he had posted sub-2 ERAs in each of his prior five seasons working out of the bullpen (2020-22, '24-25), 31 saves in 2025, as well as a 2.40 ERA in 23 starts while pitching out of the rotation in 2023.

That's a remarkable level of success for a pitcher who stands just 5-foot-8. Marcus Stroman is the only MLB pitcher this century who stood that height or shorter to have made as many as 10 starts. Taira's extension -- measuring the distance from the pitching rubber that the pitcher releases the baseball -- is regarded as elite, however, and to a point where he'd likely rank in the upper quarter in U.S. play in that department. Between that and his six -- and, by some accounts, as many as eight -- pitches in his repertoire, he counters the height question with a great deal of upside. Taira's command of his pitch mix is considered elite, and generally ground ball-generating, so even with some anticipated regression to his strikeout rate he might well deliver numbers that place among the top 40 pitchers in fantasy baseball.

We'll see how swiftly and smoothly Taira adapts to U.S. play, which despite becoming less demanding upon starting pitchers in the post-COVID era, still has a lengthier and more physically taxing schedule. Questions about whether he's more suited for relief than rotation work are valid, and the primary obstacle towards him earning that potential top-40 starter ranking. By signing in Toronto, where he's more likely to have the team's patience with his adapting to the rotation, Saito will earn a ranking around No. 75 at the position, in the Joey Cantillo/Trey Yesavage/Eduardo Rodriguez range. -- Cockcroft (11/24)

Freddy Peralta signs with Orioles
Peralta, 30, ended the 2026 season with a bloated 4.42 ERA and 1.33 WHIP, but those numbers hardly tell the story. The longtime Brewers ace who struck out 200 hitters during three consecutive seasons started the 2026 season with the Mets after an offseason trade, and things went poorly right away. Then, months later, the Mets traded Peralta to the Rays and, voila, all was well again!

With his mechanics tweaked and his approach refined (more changeups, fewer sliders), Peralta posted a 3.25 ERA and 1.01 WHIP during 10 Rays starts, albeit with a lower strikeout rate than typical, but at least he was good. Then he thrived in the postseason, winning ALCS MVP honors. That is what fantasy managers expect. Peralta may not be a top 20 starting pitcher for fantasy, but he should be close. Peralta ranks among the top 100 players for points and roto formats. -- Karabell (11/24)

Trevor Rogers signs with Cubs
Rogers, 29, was never going to match his incredible 2025 season, when he posted a 1.81 ERA and 0.90 WHIP during 18 starts, but his 2026 campaign (4.03, 1.18) may have still exceeded some expectations. After all, the 6-foot-5 left-hander posted a 4.92 ERA and 1.58 WHIP for the Marlins and Orioles in 2024. The 2017 first-round pick dealt with injuries, control issues and inconsistency for much of his career, among other things. Then, suddenly, he was a star, even for half a season.

Rogers probably isn't a star. The Cubs get a guy who made 30 starts (for the first time) and did his best work in the second half, with a 3.52 ERA and 1.04 WHIP, whiffing 27% of hitters. That's good, reliable work, and Rogers was among the top 40 starting pitchers in ESPN fantasy points. Can the Cubs and fantasy managers get that version in 2027? That seems reasonable. Rogers isn't an ace, but worthy of being among the top 40 starters in drafts. There is nothing wrong with that. -- Karabell (11/24)

Tarik Skubal signs with Mets

Two winters ago, the New York Mets opened their wallet to get their offensive centerpiece, Juan Soto. On Sunday, the Mets did the same to get a centerpiece for their rotation, and for a similarly record-setting deal, signing Tarik Skubal to a nine-year, $450 million contract.

Fortunately for us in fantasy, we won't need to spend as much as the Mets did to add Skubal to our rosters, but it's a good landing spot for the lefty. He'll call one of the more pitching-leaning ballparks in Citi Field his home through 2036. -- Cockcroft (11/23)

For a more in-depth look at the fantasy impact of Skubal's signing, click here.

Luis Castillo and Davis Martin traded to Rockies
What happens when the league's worst non-Rockies or Athletics pitcher (minimum 130 innings) comes to Coors Field? We're about to find out. Castillo entered 2026 riding a four-year streak with at least 350 fantasy points, 160 strikeouts and a sub-1.20 WHIP. However, a progressive drop in his velocity and a rise in his fly ball rate during that time caused him to unravel last year, first for the Seattle Mariners and then catastrophically so following his midseason trade to the Chicago White Sox. Castillo's year ended with a shoulder injury, so in addition to the Coors factor, he enters 2027 facing many questions.

Martin, meanwhile, was the far superior fantasy pitcher between these two -- by almost two times in terms of point production (242-127). Martin, though, ended 2026 on a similarly sour note. He had a 9-2 record and 2.41 ERA through his first 13 starts, but went 0-8 with a 5.72 ERA thereafter. He dealt with a calf issue, a blister and concerns that he might be tipping pitches, ultimately making only a mop-up appearance during Chicago's playoff run.

Martin was nevertheless the piece the Rockies wanted in order to agree to absorb Castillo's remaining contract. Both will probably eat innings for a Rockies rotation always in need of depth. Either could be a "matchup candidate" in road games, if they seem to have righted the ship during spring training -- which is why a lockout-influenced, shortened preseason would be detrimental to both. Still, neither pitcher is a draft-day option, given their new team. -- Cockcroft (11/20)

Twins sign Sonny Gray
Gray, now 37 years old, returns to Minnesota after a three-year detour through St. Louis and Boston. He has enjoyed a bit of a career rebirth later in his career, averaging 385.8 fantasy points over the past four seasons, and never deviating by more than 25 points in either direction in any individual year. Gray's consistency is a valuable thing in fantasy leagues, particularly points-based scoring, where his good ratios and solid innings totals are most advantageous.

That said, a two-year pattern of declining average fastball velocity and strikeout rates raises concerns that regression might hit him harder than a typical frontline starter, if not in 2027 then perhaps if he doesn't opt out and continues into his 39-year-old campaign in 2028. I've got Gray ranked amongst my top 25 fantasy starting pitchers, and within the top 75 overall, and I'd expect he will (and should) generally be drafted in that range.

Gray's acquisition, however, gives the Twins at least nine viable rotation candidates, creating a logjam of popular deep-mixed/AL-only names like Mick Abel, Zebby Matthews, Connor Prielipp for fourth/fifth starter spots. Perhaps a trade is forthcoming, preferably for some hitting to bolster the lineup and give Gray more run support, but otherwise this is a spring battle that'll be high on the list of those to watch. Only Gray, Joe Ryan, Taj Bradley and Pablo Lopez would figure to be locks. -- Cockcroft (11/18)

Bryce Miller traded to Royals
Miller, 28, emerged as a standout fantasy option for the Seattle Mariners in 2024, winning 12 games and posting a 2.94 ERA and 0.98 WHIP. Injuries and inconsistency have plagued the right-hander since then, as Miller won only eight of 39 starts in 2025-26 with a 4.82 ERA and 1.26 WHIP while permitting 38 home runs. Elbow woes ruined his 2025 campaign, and he missed the first six weeks of 2026 with an oblique injury.

Still, when Miller is healthy, he can be effective. He posted a 2.18 ERA and 0.83 WHIP prior to the 2026 All-Star break before a rough second half (and myriad home runs) ruined things. Moving from one pitcher's park in Seattle to another in Kansas City shouldn't be a factor, but at least Miller should be guaranteed a rotation spot, which was in question in Seattle. Miller is certainly a sleeper candidate to regain his place among the top 30 starting pitchers in fantasy, but ESPN's preliminary points ranking features Miller well outside the top 50 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/18)

Dustin May signs with White Sox

May, 29, made 31 mostly league-average starts for the Cardinals and eventual champion Brewers this season -- many of them quite abbreviated. In fact, he ended up averaging fewer than four innings over his 10 Brewers starts and he did not qualify for the ERA title. The desperate White Sox figure to allow May to go deeper into games, but that comes at a cost, since he posted a 4.70 ERA and a 1.32 WHIP with only 0.4 bWAR last season.

Hey, at least May stayed healthy, which is a feat for him. Plus, he was a bit unlucky, as his 3.54 FIP indicates. However, that doesn't mean May warrants inclusion in ESPN standard drafts, with a preliminary points-league rank outside the top 75 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/18)

Other free agents: Michael King, Robbie Ray, Brandon Woodruff, Zac Gallen, Shota Imanaga, Chris Bassitt, Jack Flaherty, Jameson Taillon, Max Scherzer, Clay Holmes, Matthew Boyd, Nick Pivetta, Shane Bieber, Nick Martinez, Tyler Mahle, Michael Soroka

Relief pitcher
Emilio Pagan signs with Tigers
Pagan, 35, saved 57 games for the Cincinnati Reds over the past two seasons, although his 2025 numbers were rather ordinary (3.38 ERA, 25.9% K rate). Still, this is a franchise that desired Kenley Jansen and let him save 22 games last season even though there were better pitchers in the bullpen. Pagan produced nearly identical stats to Jansen. In other words, Pagan isn't so valuable -- but if all you care about are saves in a roto format, a healthy Pagan should provide at least 25 of them. -- Karabell (11/13)

Evan Phillips signs with Braves
Phillips, 32, posted a 2.36 ERA over parts of six seasons for the Los Angeles Dodgers. He also accrued 42 combined saves during 2023 and 2024. He missed most of 2025 dealing with Tommy John surgery and returned last season to pitch 26 effective innings. Additionally, Phillips has never permitted a run over 18⅓ postseason innings. The Braves figure to turn to Robert Suarez to close (because Raisel Iglesias is a free agent), but a healthy Phillips should accrue ample holds as well as occasional saves. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Raisel Iglesias, Pete Fairbanks, Carlos Estevez, A.J. Minter, Blake Treinen, Martin Perez, Gregory Soto, Kenley Jansen, Hiromi Itoh (posted)

stories.headline: How do MLS' European-bred stars adjust to the playoffs? 'It's a challenge'
stories.summary: For MLS' biggest stars, they've spent their careers crowning champions based on the table. For them, adapting to the idea of the playoffs isn't easy.
stories.body:
After a stop-start, nine-month regular season, the MLS Cup playoffs are here, and for players, now is when the real work begins. The 34 games played between February and early November are a distant memory, useful for qualifying clubs for the postseason, but now is the competition that matters.

For European-bred stars joining the North American league, the playoffs are a curiosity, a novelty. After all, in the biggest domestic competitions across the Old World, the champion is the team that picks up the most points over the course of the campaign. So, in their new surrounds, does the regular season matter? How do players adjust to the postseason? Should teams focus solely on making a run to MLS Cup and disregard the Supporters' Shield?

All questions that don't have one single answer. Still, newcomers have their opinions. Former LA Galaxy superstar Zlatan Ibrahimovic called the system "s---" in 2019, while Inter Miami CF midfielder Rodrigo De Paul made headlines for saying that winning MLS Cup is harder than lifting the UEFA Champions League trophy.

MLS' current playoff format takes the top seven teams from each conference, while teams in eighth and ninth face off in a wild card match. The winners of the one-game play-in then complete the 16-team postseason field. Those 16 teams then contest the best-of-three Round 1 series, before the winners go on to the single-elimination conference semifinals, conference finals and MLS Cup.

"You play 34 games and then the real business starts," San Jose Earthquakes forward Timo Werner said to ESPN.

How big of an adjustment is the postseason?
The transition can be difficult for newcomers joining from a traditional football structure.

Goalkeeper Roman Bürki moved to St. Louis City in 2023 after a decorated career spent at Borussia Dortmund, SC Freiburg and four clubs in Switzerland. St. Louis made history by becoming the first expansion team to win their first four matches and conclude the regular season in first place of the Western Conference.

The team looked to be set up for success, but their playoff run told a different story. St. Louis fell to eighth-place Sporting Kansas City in just two matches in Round 1.

Frustration and shock filled the dressing room following the first loss. Players looked defeated even before traveling for the second match of the series.

"I remember being very, very tired in my head because it was my first time playing a whole year without a real break," Bürki told ESPN. "Back then, we played from January into November and so on. I just remember being mentally very tired.

"We were winning a lot and we had confidence and everything, and then towards the end of the season, like you could see the energy level was lower and lower and like it's just so hard for me to adapt to. I'm not new to playing a lot of games. In Europe we also played cup, played league games, we played in Champions League, but then at some point you had a break for at least three weeks. Something like this and just to keep going, it was very hard for me and hard to adjust."

Werner, who joined San Jose in January after playing in the Bundesliga and Premier League, was similarly concerned about exhaustion prior to his first ever MLS Cup playoffs.

"It's difficult because also at the end of the season, after a long year, you're tired," he said. "You think you are over the finish line, but no, we are not over the finish line. We still have the best to come, so it's a challenge. It is a challenge to be mentally focused on that, because knowing that the real deal is coming after the season, after the 34 games."

A less-important regular season?
Former Inter Miami defender Jordi Alba called the league's postseason "unfair" in 2024 after falling to Atlanta United in the first round after winning the Supporters' Shield and setting the record for most points in a single regular season.

Miami entered that postseason as the clear favorite with a star-studded roster, a historic 22W-8D-4L record and a three-game winning streak. But the league's ultimate glamor club fell in three games to Atlanta in a shocking upset.

"This format seems a little unfair to me," Alba said. "It is clear that it has been done this way for many years, but if you ask me, if it were up to me, I would have to be the champion of one conference against the champion of the other, to make it as fair as possible, that's how it is."

The format left Alba questioning whether the regular season even mattered.

MLS rewards the winner of the regular season with the Supporters' Shield and homefield advantage throughout the playoffs, but to most in and around the league, the Shield trails MLS Cup in importance, devaluing the effort of consistency throughout the season.

Ibrahimovic criticized the league's format for encouraging complacency during the regular season. After decades of playing for Europe's biggest clubs and sharpening a famously competitive attitude, the Swedish striker was appalled by a format he thought rewarded mediocrity.

"When you talk about the playoffs, we just need to make the playoffs, win the playoffs and that's it," Ibrahimovic said in 2019. "It doesn't matter if you lose or win [during regular season]. How can you learn mentality if you just need to learn the playoffs? I think the system is s--- ... Here you are in seventh place, you make the playoffs and you win. So, how do you create that mentality to be on your toes 24 hours a day? It's very difficult."

And now, since the number of clubs that qualify increased from six teams in each conference in 2018 to eight teams plus a play-in match in 2023, players feel an even lesser sense of urgency.

"It doesn't matter as much if you lose games in the regular season because the most important thing is making the playoffs, right?" Bürki said. "Seattle played like an average regular season [in 2024], but towards the end, they started to perform and make the playoffs and went to the first two rounds. And that's just the way you probably should approach the whole season.

"I wouldn't say it's meaningless, the regular season, but because you have that format, you don't necessarily need to get upset as much as when you don't win. In Europe, we have 34 games and that's it to win the trophy, and every game counts. Here, not every game counts the same way."

He isn't wrong. Seattle kicked off the 2024 campaign with just two wins in their first 11 matches before picking up momentum toward the end of the season and eventually reaching the Western Conference final.

The pattern continued in the first games of this year's Round 1. Supporters' Shield winners and new record points holders Nashville SC were upset by ninth-seeded FC Cincinnati, 1-0. Inter Miami, the No. 2 seed in the East, were dropped 3-0 by No. 7 seed Columbus.

Best-of-three frustrations
In a traditional two-legged tie, the scoreline in Miami would have conditioned the hosts to make every second count, but not in MLS. Instead, head coach Cristian Gonzalez took out Luis Suárez at halftime, replaced crucial midfielder Yannick Bright with recent academy signing Alex Shaw in the 62nd minute and substituted recently injured Fricio Caicedo for Telasco Segovia with more than 20 minutes left to be played.

With no aggregate score or goal difference to worry about, the Herons now enter Friday's Game 2 with a clean slate, know that the narrowest of wins will send the series to a decisive third game.

"You can lose the first game 5-0 and tie the next two games, win in PKs and you're going through? I don't like that," Seattle Sounders goalkeeper Stefan Frei said in 2024. Charlotte FC manager Dean Smith, who previously coached in the Premier League, criticized the league over the lack of impact a massive victory can have in the most crucial point of the season.

"I think if it's over too late and you win on goal differential, I think that should be it," he said in 2024. "The fact that you can go win 6-0 away and then draw at home and still not get through, it bothers me a little bit."

Sources told ESPN the best-of-three format will be eliminated in 2027, but for now teams must prepare for three potential first-round games.

The format may change over time but the playoffs will continue to be an integral part of MLS, whether its biggest European newcomers like it or not. It's up to players to find a way to adjust in order to reach the highest success in the North American league: MLS Cup.

stories.headline: Sparks forward Cameron Brink, Ben Felter wed at Stanford
stories.summary: The couple met in 2021 and was engaged in 2024 before marrying at their alma mater's Memorial Church.
stories.body:
Cameron Brink and Ben Felter have officially tied the knot after holding a ceremony on Nov. 14 at their alma mater Stanford's Memorial Church.

According to a report Tuesday from Vogue Magazine, which shared behind-the-scenes details and images, the Los Angeles Sparks forward had four bridal looks, including a custom dress from bridal designer Danielle Frankel for the ceremony, and another for the reception.

Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha, were among those in attendance. Curry and Brink are godsiblings as their fathers were teammates at Virginia Tech, and their mothers were roommates on campus.

The reception was at Ritz-Carlton, Half Moon Bay, while vows were exchanged at Memorial Church, one of the earliest interdenominational churches in the West. The waiting list to get married there can be up to four years, but alumni receive a shorter period, according to Vogue. The couple told the magazine that they always knew they wanted to wed there.

"Walking past the ornate mosaics on my way to class was always the best part of my day," Brink said.

Brink and Felter met at Stanford in the fall of 2020. The two began dating in March 2021 after Felter sent Brink an email in which he included his phone number. Felter, who rowed at Stanford, proposed to Brink in Paris in September 2024.

The No. 2 pick in the 2024 WNBA draft, Brink averaged a career-high 9.5 points plus five rebounds and 1.8 blocks for Los Angeles in the 2026 season.

If you've ever worn a UFC light heavyweight championship belt, watch out for Navajo Stirling.

His two most recent victories have come against former 205-pound champions, both knockouts. After a first-round finish of Jan Blachowicz in August, the New Zealander knocked out Jiří Procházka in Saturday's UFC Fight Night main event in Qatar.

As a result, Stirling leapfrogs Procházka in the ESPN divisional rankings, rising to No. 3 at light heavyweight. After his fourth straight knockout overall, Stirling (12-0) is right behind the division's champion, Carlos Ulberg, Stirling's training partner at City Kickboxing in Auckland. The No. 1 ranking belongs to former champion Magomed Ankalaev, who called out Stirling after Saturday's fight.

The weekend's UFC fights also led to changes in the featherweight and men's flyweight top 10s. Aljamain Sterling lost a 145-pound fight to Kevin Vallejos and drops four spots to No. 7, right below Vallejos. At 125 pounds, Kyoji Horiguchi moves up one position to No. 6 after beating Asu Almabayev, who remains 10th.

stories.headline: 'Can't judge them': who Papenhuyzen wants at the Storm
stories.summary: Ex-Melbourne star Ryan Papenhuyzen has made some big calls on who should be the next Storm coach and the one to keep from Cameron Munster and Harry Grant.
stories.body:
Ryan Papenhuyzen empathises with Cameron Munster but believes Melbourne must prioritise keeping Harry Grant if the NRL powerhouse can't hold on to both superstars.

Munster on Tuesday rejected an offer from the Storm believed to be for one year with the option of another season, labelling the terms "disappointing".

The Storm are also fighting to keep Grant, and Papenhuyzen was unequivocal when asked on Wednesday who the club should target if salary-cap pressures meant only one of the newly crowned Australian World Cup winners could stay.

"I went through something similar as Munster where I thought the club had low-balled me," the happily retired 2020 premiership-winning hero told AAP.

"But having my time out of the game now, they've got their reasons for offering those certain amounts and it might not be enough (for Munster).

"Penrith have done it for years and years. They get to a point where they can't hold their players and they've got a price for their players.

"So I understand Munster's perspective. He wants to earn as much as he can in his career and he wants to win a premiership, so that probably limits his opportunities.

"If a club's got money and they're in a premiership window, it's probably a good chance he'll go to that club."

At 28, skipper Grant is four years younger than Munster and more important long-term to the Storm, Papenhuyzen believes.

"Harry's done a brilliant job in terms of leadership," the ex-Clive Churchill Medallist turned caddy said after playing in the Australian PGA Championship pro-am in Sydney.

"The amount of care he has for everyone in that group and the way he thinks about the game, I feel really sorry for him over the last 12 months (when Melbourne missed the finals) because he's always trying to find new ideas to bring everyone.

"He's a great leader for that club going forward. I'd hate to see him go because he's a player you want to build a club around and I guess Munster is towards the back end of his career.

"He had a great World Cup, but World Cups are different to NRL seasons. You've got to lock in for a month with that, and an NRL season's a long time."

Pressed on who he'd keep as a priority, Papenhuyzen said: "Harry's probably the one leadership-wise. Just his qualities are really admirable.

"You know what Munster brings to the game. He gives you confidence standing next to him, knowing what he's going do, but I just think Harry ..."

With coach Craig Bellamy confirming he is moving on at the end of 2027, Papenhuyzen also suspects Grant might be a better for the Storm's new mentor, whomever that may be.

"Harry's really respected and in terms of trying to keep the culture, he's very open-minded too," the BMW golf correspondent said.

"He's open to new ideas, whereas Munster is very much like Bellamy - he's sort of got his way and it's worked for him for so long.

"Whatever they both decide to do, you can't judge them. It's never a right or wrong decision."

Papenhuyzen believes it would be "awesome" if Billy Slater succeeded Bellamy, but suspects "life is too good" for the Storm legend to be a head NRL coach.

"I love Jyles. If he went back there, I'd be awfully encouraged of how well they're going to go. They'd probably be my two."

But Papenhuyzen, also open to helping out the new coach, nominated Bellamy's son Aaron as a left-field option.

"Aaron's awesome with people," he said.

"He's awesome with the wider playing group and he understands that Craig sometimes pushes the boundaries. Aaron's a bit more like Wendy - Craig's, Craig's wife.

"They're both a bit more more gentle, so you've got that loving, nurturing side and potentially (he could do the job).

"I do know you just need people around you. We'd be silly to say the coach controls everything."

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Your guide to the all-day, 15-game hockey bonanza on Black Friday
stories.summary: Find game previews, betting intel, broadcast information, stats and highlights here.
stories.body:
We have reached the apex of a wondrous week for hockey fans. With no games Thursday, there were 14 games Wednesday, now 15 on Friday followed by 13 on Saturday.

What's more, the Friday calendar is an extra special treat, with 12 of those 15 games starting before 7 p.m. ET, evenly spaced throughout the afternoon. So it can be done!

So what's on tap in each of those matchups? Read on for a look at what you need to know for the games, including betting info and broadcast details.

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Toronto Maple Leafs at Boston Bruins

1 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | BOS -166, O/U: 6.5

What better way to kick off a full day of hockey than with an Original Six showdown in Boston.

These two teams have met 695 times in the regular season, with the B's holding a 311-272-112 edge. It is the first of four games that the Atlantic Division foes will play against one another this season.

It's tough to find a metric in which the Maple Leafs are better than the Bruins, and thus Boston is 10 points ahead of Toronto in the standings. The Leafs do have a slightly better power play (25.4% to 20.0%) and penalty kill (82.3% to 80.0%) than the Bruins, so there's that!

Boston is both scoring more goals per game (3.50 to 3.15) and allowing fewer (2.71 to 3.46).

One thing the teams have in common is that one player leads their respective team in both goals and assists; for Toronto it's Auston Matthews (14 goals, 20 assists), and for Boston it's David Pastrnak (11 goals, 21 assists).

Calgary Flames at New Jersey Devils

1 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NJ -265, O/U: 6.5

As the current No. 2 seed in the Metro Division at American Thanksgiving, the Devils are right where many had projected. It'll be tough to catch the Hurricanes for first, but they're at least withing striking distance.

Calgary has exceeded the expectations of most prognosticators and sit fourth in the Pacific coming out of the Thanksgiving break. Behind the Oilers and Golden Knights, it's seemingly anyone's race for the No. 3 seed, and hey, stranger things have happened than a team like this getting lucky and earning that spot.

This is the first of two matchups between the clubs this season (they'll play again on Jan. 30 in Calgary). As with the Bruins and Leafs, the Devils lead the Flames in most categories right now except for special teams, where Calgary has an edge in both the power play (25.8% to 19.8%) and penalty kill (80.0% to 67.8%).

Utah Mammoth at Nashville Predators

1 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | UTA -112, O/U: 6.5

The two clubs enter this outing with just two points (but three spots in the standings) separating them.

Nashville defeated Dallas on Wednesday and sits fourth in the Central with 31 points. Utah outlasted Minnesota on Wednesday and is seventh.

A big part of the Mammoth's struggles of late is health; a group that includes Nick Schmaltz, John Marino and Nate Schmidt remains sidelined. The Preds are comparatively quite healthy, with no one listed on the injury report.

This is the first of four matchups between the teams this season. Utah won three of four in 2025-26, and a win here could get them back on track after an uneven November.

Dallas Stars at St. Louis Blues

2 p.m. ET (NHL Network) | DAL -142, O/U: 5.5

This will be Game 2 of the season series between these division rivals, after the Blues took a 4-0 decision in Dallas back on Oct. 2.

St. Louis has won three straight games at home, all of which were against teams currently in playoff position (Anaheim, New Jersey and Edmonton). Dallas has won two straight road tilts -- both of which were in Vegas.

The Stars are led in scoring this season by Mikko Rantanen (10 goals, 18 assists), while the perennially underrated Robert Thomas leads the way for the Blues (five goals, 20 assists).

Ottawa Senators at Tampa Bay Lightning

3 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | TB -135, O/U: 5.5

This one is in the mix as the game of the day, with the Atlantic Division's first-place Senators (35 points through 26 games) taking on the second-place Lightning (32 through 24).

It's the first matchup of the season for these division rivals, and the Senators won two out of three last season.

Up front, the Lightning are paced this season by Nikita Kucherov (10 goals, 23 assists), while the Sens are led by Tim Stutzle (13 goals, 18 assists).

The critical matchup is in the crease, where Ottawa's Linus Ullmark leads the NHL in both goals-against average (1.63) and save percentage (.935). On the opposite end, Andrei Vasilevskiy is a bit behind in both metrics (2.56, .897), but does have his name on the Stanley Cup twice, compared with zero times for Ullmark.

Vancouver Canucks at Philadelphia Flyers

3 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | PHI -230, O/U: 6.5

These two clubs met back on Nov. 9 during the Flyers' West Coast swing, a 3-1 victory for Philly. Does Vancouver get some revenge in its visit to eastern Pennsylvania?

If so, it'll be without Elias Pettersson, whose bounce-back season has been interrupted by an upper-body injury that has knocked him out until after the team's road trip is over.

The Flyers had started to generate some momentum with a three-game win streak, but that was ended with a 7-3 loss to the Capitals on Wednesday.

Florida Panthers at Washington Capitals

3 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | WSH -108, O/U: 6.5

These teams came into the season with playoff expectations -- and both are out of the picture as the post-Thanksgiving era begins.

Florida has the benefit of the nascent return of both Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, who returned on Wednesday. That helped spark a 5-3 win over the visiting Senators.

Washington will be without Jordan Kyrou for the next bit and must continue to rely on fellow newcomer Alex Tuch, who leads the team in goals (15) and points (20).

Alex Ovechkin still has just one goal through 22 games. He didn't score that goal in the previous game against the Panthers but has 45 in his 78 career games against Florida.

Detroit Red Wings at Columbus Blue Jackets

3 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CBJ -130, O/U: 5.5

The Red Wings are 1-0-0 in the post-Dylan Larkin Era, rolling over the Canucks 5-1 on Wednesday following the trade late Sunday night.

Meanwhile, the Blue Jackets are coming in off two straight losses to the Devils and could be involved in the trade market again at some point too.

Neither team is particularly close to the playoff race right now -- the second wild card has 31 points, while Detroit (21) and Columbus (19) are well behind -- but perhaps whichever club wins this one will use it as a springboard to a big run from here on out.

Colorado Avalanche at Minnesota Wild

4 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MIN -125, O/U: 6.5

Another candidate for game of the day, with two teams that have legitimate Stanley Cup hopes squaring off in a divisional showdown.

Minnesota comes out of the Thanksgiving break with a nine-point cushion ahead of second-place Dallas in the Central, and a 10-point edge over Colorado; both of the chasing teams have three games in hand.

The Avs and Wild have not yet played this regular season, and the last time they faced off was an epic showdown in the second round of the 2026 playoffs. The Avs took the series 4-1, and perhaps there's some residual angst on both sides.

Although the Avs will not have Nathan MacKinnon for this game, their other superstar Cale Makar did return back to action this week. The Wild will be without blueliner Quinn Hughes for this game but have one of the league's top scorers (Kirill Kaprizov) and goaltenders (Jesper Wallstedt) ready to roll.

After this matchup, the teams don't meet again until March 17.

Los Angeles Kings at Anaheim Ducks

4 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | LA -120, O/U: 6.5

Sometimes the Battle of California showdowns have quite a bit on the line. Other times, one team is considerably better than the other.

We're in one of the latter phases this time around, with the Ducks sitting third in the Pacific with 25 points through 26 games while the Kings are seventh, with 18 in 22.

Nevertheless, the "lesser" team sometimes gets extra motivated in these rivalry showdowns, so don't count the Kings out. That's particularly true following the return of Artemi Panarin, who leads the Kings across the board in scoring with eight goals and 12 assists.

That's a bit behind the leading scorer on the Ducks, Cutter Gauthier, whose breakout campaign continues. Gauthier enters this game with 23 goals and nine assists on the season.

Vegas Golden Knights at San Jose Sharks

4 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | VGK -205, O/U: 6.5

Speaking of somewhat dormant rivalries, this used to be one of the best in the Western Conference. Unfortunately, the Sharks have fallen off a bit from those days in the late 2010s, while the Golden Knights continue to dominate.

Entering this matchup, Vegas is second in the Pacific with 35 points through 26 games, while the Sharks are fifth with 24 through 27.

Macklin Celebrini (10 goals, 21 assists) is San Jose's leading scorer this season, while Jack Eichel (11 goals, 22 assists) holds the top spot on Vegas' leaderboard.

New York Rangers at Chicago Blackhawks

5:30 p.m. ET (TNT) | NYR -175, O/U: 6.5

Although these two Original Six teams are at disparate sides of the contention cycle -- the Rangers are right in the Eastern wild-card mix while the Blackhawks are near the Western basement -- they enter this matchup trending in opposite directions.

Chicago has won three straight (albeit against other non-playoff teams) and has points in six of its last seven. New York got pasted in its last two, a 5-2 loss to the Hurricanes on Sunday and a 5-1 loss to the Sabres on Wednesday.

Can Alexis Lafreniere, Adam Fox & Co. get things back on track on Friday? Or will it be another W for the Blackhawks?

Winnipeg Jets at New York Islanders

7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NYI -135, O/U: 6.5

This will be the second and final matchup between these two teams this season (unless, of course, they meet in the Stanley Cup Final), after the Jets won 4-3 in an overtime thriller on Nov. 19.

Ahead of this contest, both teams are in playoff position, as the Jets currently hold the second Western wild card with 30 points through 26 games while the Isles are third in the Metro with 29 points through 24 games.

In the first game, the Jets managed to do what most teams have not this season: keep Matthew Schaefer off the scoresheet. Does that continue in this one?

Pittsburgh Penguins at Buffalo Sabres

8 p.m. ET (TNT) | BUF -148, O/U: 6.5

A pair of 2026 playoff teams that -- as play starts Friday -- are not headed back to the promised land in 2027.

Pittsburgh has a significantly steeper hill to climb, with 16 points through 24 games and increasing buzz that Erik Karlsson (let alone the big three of Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin and Kris Letang) could be traded to a contender ahead of the deadline.

Buffalo has 26 points through 25 games, which means they're five behind the second wild card. As opposed to trading players away, many have speculated that their GM, Jarmo Kekalainen, might be on the hunt for a big-ticket trade to improve his roster before it's too late.

This is the first of three meetings between the clubs this season after the Pens won two of three in 2025-26. Tage Thompson (17 goals, 13 assists) leads the Sabres in scoring, while Malkin (seven goals, 13 assists) is atop the Penguins' leaderboard.

Seattle Kraken at Edmonton Oilers

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | EDM -205, O/U: 6.5

In the nightcap, the Oilers' dynamic trio (Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard) welcome the Kraken to Edmonton again after defeating them 3-1 on Oct. 3.

Edmonton currently holds the No. 1 seed in the Pacific, with 38 points through 27 games. The Kraken are right in the battle for the No. 3 seed -- though they're currently two points back with 23 points through 22 games.

McDavid leads everyone in scoring this season with 59 points; Draisaitl (47) and Bouchard (41) are third and fourth. Seattle's scoring leader Berkly Catton is tied for 88th with 19.

stories.headline: Pochettino defends his Man United management style: 'I'm not nice'
stories.summary: Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has hit back at criticism of his management style by insisting: "I am not nice."
stories.body:
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has hit back at criticism of his management style by insisting: "I am not nice."

Former England midfielder Jamie Redknapp, speaking on The Overlap with Tim Sherwood, accused Pochettino of being "too nice" compared to his time in charge of Southampton and Tottenham.

"When I saw Pochettino at Southampton and I saw him at Tottenham, he looked to me like he had that Argentinian dog in him," Redknapp said.

"I look at him now and he's high fiving everyone, he's got the bracelets on, he's got the barnet. I think he's gone too nice, I do."

Speaking at a news conference on Friday, Pochettino took the opportunity to bite back. The 54-year-old wasn't asked directly about Redknapp's comments and gave his response unprompted.

"Do not misunderstand my words," Pochettino said.

"Sometimes we are confusing two words that mean maybe something similar; nice and good.

"I am not nice. I am not nice. We have to be good. That is a different thing. I am not nice. I am trying to be good.

"We know when we need to push, when we need to be strong and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything. These two things are different."

Pochettino has worked his new players hard since arriving last week, implementing longer training sessions than was normal under Michael Carrick.

But he's also conscious that he needs to repair the confidence of the squad after a miserable start to the season which has seen the team slip in the Premier League's relegation zone.

- Bruno Fernandes contract extended by Man United until 2028 - sources

- Would any USMNT players really make Man United better if they followed Poch?

- Transfer rumors, news: Nico Paz open to Man United; against Real Madrid return

"I think it's easy for us because we arrived one week ago," Pochettino said.

"It's easy to arrive here with full energy and be positive and try to build that belief that we need.

"But of course for the players it's so tough because we cannot go away from all that noise that is around this football club. It's not only in this football club. It's in every single club that is not performing well. That is why it's so tough for the players."

Pochettino will lead United at Old Trafford for the first time when Brentford visit on Saturday. With such a packed schedule since his arrival last week, the Argentinian revealed he's not yet had the chance to meet Sir Alex Ferguson, one of his managerial role models.

"I didn't have the opportunity," Pochettino added.

"I send all my admiration and love to him and I promise I will send a text. Look, it's not to say nothing. It's 12, 13, 14 hours spent here in the training ground and I didn't have time. You know, we are so fully focused on trying to provide everything, to start to improve our performances."
